title: Jagdish Kaushik v. State of U.P.
coram: V.K. Shukla and Ranjana Pandya, JJ.
docket: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 10068 of 2015
disposition: s.135 FIR not quashed; arrest, if any, to follow CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A; compounding left to Supply Code 2005.
headnote: A Division Bench refused to quash an FIR under s.135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 because it disclosed a cognizable offence. Arrest not having been made, the Court directed that if arrest is contemplated for an offence not entailing more than seven years' imprisonment, police must comply with CrPC ss.41(1)(b) and 41-A. If the offence is compoundable, the accused may seek compounding under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Jagdish Kaushik invoked the Allahabad High Court's criminal writ jurisdiction to quash the FIR dated 20 March 2015, registered as Case Crime Nos. 181–182 of 2015 under s.135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 at Police Station Kosi, District Mathura. He had not been arrested. Counsel submitted that a proved offence under s.135 could not attract more than seven years' imprisonment, so arrest should not be mechanical, and that the alleged offence was compoundable. The State and the other respondents appeared.

holding_units.topic: quashing of s.135 FIR; arrest safeguards; compounding
holding_units.holding: An FIR under s.135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 that discloses a cognizable offence will not be quashed. Where arrest has not been made and the offence cannot carry more than seven years' imprisonment, any arrest must comply with CrPC ss.41(1)(b) and 41-A; if the offence is compoundable the accused may seek compounding under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

principle_tags.application: s.135 FIR disclosing a cognizable offence left intact; any arrest must follow CrPC 41(1)(b)/41-A; compounding, if available, to be sought under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

not_decided.point: Whether the alleged s.135 offence is in fact compoundable and whether compounding should be granted
not_decided.note: Petitioner left to seek compounding under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 if available.
